per_example.input: Synthesize the evolutionary trajectory of retrieval augmentation from static index lookups to end-to-end trained models.
per_example.reference: Key entities: BM25, Dense Passage Retrieval, Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Expected facts: evolution, BM25, differentiable, end-to-end, joint training.
per_example.adapter_output: Early retrieval‑augmented generation relied on fixed, static index lookups, as highlighted by the contrast in R³AG, which notes that, unlike previous approaches, it models the dynamic alignment between queries and retriever capabilities [chunk_arxiv_2604_22849v1_001]. The next step introduced end‑to‑end training of the generator with retrieval signals through multi‑task learning and relevance label sampling, showing scalability with model size and state‑of‑the‑art performance on five of seven KILT tasks [chunk_arxiv_2207_03030v1_001]. Building on this, R³AG proposed a learnable routing framework that decomposes retriever capability into retrieval quality and generation utility and optimizes it with a contrastive objective using document assessments and answer correctness, enabling query‑specific retriever selection [chunk_arxiv_2604_22849v1_001]. Subsequent work enriched the retriever by leveraging multimodal knowledge graphs, demonstrating significant gains and new state‑of‑the‑art results on knowledge‑intensive VQA [chunk_arxiv_2508_05318v2_002]. Finally, detailed analyses of parser, chunker, and embedding choices over large regulatory corpora revealed that retrieval differences are driven mainly by ranking quality rather than information loss, highlighting the shift toward fine‑grained, end‑to‑end optimization of the entire retrieval pipeline [chunk_arxiv_2609_31660v1_001; chunk_arxiv_2609_31660v1_002].
